oar.note: Trireme sustained ~6 kn at leisurely oaring; reconstructed Olympias steady 4 kn, max 8; Xenophon's single-day Byzantium-Heraclea voyage = 7.37 kn average. Galleys rowed ~8-10 h and beached at night: 4-6 kn x 1.852 x 8 h = 60-90 km; high = Xenophon's ~240 km day.

sail.note: Casson, Ships and Seamanship in the Ancient World (ch. on speed; TAPA 82, 1951): favourable winds 4-6 kn open water (178-267 km/24 h), 3-4 kn coasting; foul winds ~2-2.5 kn (89-111 km). Mid 150 km/day mixed.

steam.note: Liberty ship ~11 kn (489 km/day); steam ship of the line 12 kn (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ship_of_the_line); slow convoys ~7 kn (311 km). Upper ~15 kn fleet cruising.

modern.note: Composite: transit speeds 12-25 kn (533-1,111 km/day); Liberty upgrade target 15 kn. Grade C.

oar.note: Triremes had to be "pulled from the water during the night" and carried little water or food; fleets depended on beaching and shore supply every 1-3 days.

sail.note: Armada planning carried "victuals for eight months" (240 days, high); sail-era warships typically 3-6 months of provisions (mid 120, composite).

steam.note: Educated guess: coal endurance 2-6 weeks at cruising speed; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_White_Fleet notes coaling as the limiting factor.

modern.note: Educated guess: conventional warships ~2-4 weeks of fuel at transit speed without underway replenishment; food ~30-90 days.
